messages:
mika: Heads-up — noticed odd billing usage for Dedicated pools in eu-west-1 this morning. Committed throughput meters show ~30% over our expected baseline for several accounts. Anyone seen this?
ryan: I saw alerts from the cost pipeline at 07:10UTC. Looks like committed_hours and actual_throughput tags diverged for a subset of customers after last night's scaler rollout.
deepa: @ryan which tag? is it the 'commit_bucket' label or the per-deployment 'reserved_tier' tag?
ryan: commit_bucket. Some VMs got the legacy tag due to a Kubernetes webhook mismatch during the rollout.
ingrid: ouch. that mismatch would cause the billing mapper to attribute requests to on-demand instead of committed pool, right?
ryan: Exactly. The meter classified consumption as uncommitted, so invoice line items spiked for those customers.
ops-bot: Deploy: reserved-pool-scaler v2 rolled to eu-west-1 at 2024-07-27T02:05:12Z by ryan.
mika: Quick numbers: total affected GPUs ~18 (mixture of A100 and A10G), estimated 24 hours of misallocation so far. Finance projection = ~$9k additional monthly if not fixed.
finance-bot: Alert: potential invoice adjustment needed. Recommend opening ticket with cloud provider if tags can't be reconciled within 48h.
deepa: I can patch the webhook to force re-tagging on pod restart, but we need consent for a rolling restart window. Any low-traffic windows today?
ingrid: EU morning looks okay for a short rolling restart. Put a 30% concurrency limit on restarts and route traffic to burst-capacity while we rotate.
ryan: I'll prepare a one-line remediation: `kubectl patch deployment reserved-pool-scaler -p '{"spec":{"template":{"metadata":{"annotations":{"retag":"force"}}}}}'` — that triggers recreated pods with correct tagging.
mika: Do that. Also we should recalc commit sizing for affected accounts — current commit sizes were provisioned based on 95th-percentile token/sec and assuming 10% headroom. After this incident, we should adopt a revised formula: baseline = p95, safety = +25% if region has high variance, plus 1 GPU buffer for H100/A100 mixes.
ingrid: Agreed. For small customers we should cap minimum commit at 0.5 GPU-equivalent and for enterprise customers present a dedicated + burst hybrid: reserved commit for steady qps, burst pool for spikes.
deepa: FYI, billing meter accepts retroactive tag reconciliation if we can produce timestamped attribution logs for the period. I'll start exporting request logs (nginx access + routing metadata) for the affected window.
ryan: For sizing exercises, I ran a quick sim: workload X (chat, avg seq 512) p95 tokens/s = 4.2k -> maps to ~3 A100s sustained. With +25% -> 3.75 -> round up to 4. If customer had 6 committed units before, we should recommend downscale to 4 and enable burst to 8 for peak.
mika: Nice. Make sure we include quantization/latency tradeoffs in the proposal — quantized variants can reduce GPU footprint but may increase tail latency.
ingrid: Operational ask: create a short checklist for renewals: (1) verify tags and metering pre-commit, (2) compute p95 from last 30 days, (3) apply regional variance multiplier, (4) propose burst buffer.
ryan: I'll open an RFC in docs and attach the simulation code snippet. Also opening a cloud billing ticket referencing invoice IDs and our export.
deepa: Rolling restart started. I'll monitor tag reconciliation and post a status update in 10m.
ops-bot: Pod restarted: reserved-pool-scaler-7f6c9 (eu-west-1)
mika: status?
deepa: After first 5 pods, tags reconciled for ~6 GPUs. Billing mapper shows reclassification events starting 07:25UTC.
ryan: Re-run the commit-sizing script on a sample affected customer to validate post-fix numbers. Using `python tools/commit_sizer.py --window=30d --pctl=95 --safety=0.25 --round=1`
mika: Action items: 1) finish webhook patch/rolling restart (deepa), 2) export logs and file billing ticket (ryan + finance-bot), 3) update renewal checklist & commit-sizing RFC (ryan + ingrid), 4) propose short-term invoice adjustment process (mika + finance-bot).
ingrid: For future prevention, let's add an admission-controller unit test that fails deployments missing commit_bucket tag.
deepa: Agreed — adding test and will include in PR.
ops-bot: Ticket created: CLOUD-INV-1191 by ryan.
ryan: Cloud provider responded — they can do a one-time invoice adjustment if we provide reconciled attribution within 72h. Need logs and a short reconciliation plan.
mika: Good. Keep the size recommendations conservative while we do the audit. We'll present to customer success before any automatic downscales.
ingrid: tiny follow-up: consider region-specific multipliers — eu-west historical variance = 1.25, us-west = 1.15, ap-southeast = 1.4. Add to RFC.
finance-bot: Noted. Estimated exposure if not reconciled: $9.3k/mo; if provider adjusts invoice we can recover ~85%.
mika: Thanks team. Post-mortem to follow after invoice outcome.
ryan: 10-4 — will keep thread updated.
